column1: # Queries the catalogue runs that the TraceQL corpus does not contain.
# The corpus at crates/pulsus-traceql/tests/corpus/ is the parser's, and it was
# written to cover the GRAMMAR. Twelve rules of server-implementation.md 3.2 are
# ones no corpus query exercises, so the catalogue's comparison could not tell a
# right rule from a wrong one for them, whatever its agreement count said. Each
# row below is one such rule, with the query that reaches it and what it decides.
# They are counted separately from the corpus's 141 and answered the same way:
# `functional-requirements.md`'s T-C8 state the number in prose, so both move
# when a row is added here.
# each row is answered and compared exactly as the corpus's queries are.

column3: what it decides

a search grouped by an ATTRIBUTE, which 3.2 says is served; the corpus groups only by `name` and `resource.service.name`, both String columns, so no corpus query renders a group key read from the JSON
a group key no span carries: every span groups under `nil` (`docs/api.md` §4.2), one spanset per trace

a group key whose value has the same TEXT at two stored types on one trace — `1` as an integer on one span and `1.0` as a double on another — so a statement that groups on the label alone merges two groups the API keeps apart (`docs/api.md` §4.2: an attribute by-key renders in the arm the sender stored it as)
a trace with more than one group, whose first-appearance order differs from the group values' own order (trace six: `Az` starts before `A\n`)
the SPAN-SCOPED branch of the truthiness rule; the corpus's only truthiness query is unscoped
`| coalesce()` with a group key to drop; the corpus's `| coalesce()` query has no `by()` before it
`topk` over more than one series; the corpus's topk query has one series on this fixture, so the two orders keep the same one
the same, in the other direction
a `span:id` comparison with an id a fixture span HAS; the corpus's three compare a sixteen-character id with a four-character literal, so their answer is empty whichever column the rule reads

a comparison whose selection and baseline are BOTH non-empty, over a resource carried by spans on both sides, with a `topN` small enough that applying it per key and per side differs from applying it once

the other side of the comparison above: its selection carries the spans with events, links and instrumentation attributes, which `compare_both_sides` has only on its baseline — between them the five scopes appear on both sides, so a rule that puts one scope's rows on the wrong side cannot hide in a scope that only ever has one
`with(exemplars=false)`, the one hint that changes a read; no corpus query turns exemplars off
a negated condition that holds on `…05`
presence spelled as a negated absence
an attribute `avg()` over int and double
an aggregate after `by()`, each group its own
two aggregate stages, two entries
`select()` of an event attribute
a `duration` key, Go duration text
a `traceDuration` key
trace order taken before the later filter
only the first event of `…06`
`!=` over two events that disagree
the negation of a one-of-two event match
only the second link of `…06`
`!=` over two links that disagree
the negation of a one-of-two link match
an event intrinsic, the first of two events
`!=` on a link intrinsic, two links
literal on the left, second event only
literal on the left, second link only
an event intrinsic, literal on the left
`!=` on a link intrinsic, literal left
a negative link match projects nothing
a negative event match projects nothing
field against field `!=`, one type
field against field over two types
two parentless spans are not siblings
a resource value stored as an integer, projected: on a cluster the lookup crosses to each shard as a literal, which must keep the stored type (#600 part 2)
the same value as a group key: re-typed, it fails the presence rule and every span falls into the missing-key group (#600 part 2)
`select()` of an event attribute on `…06`, whose two events hold it: the last, `IOError`, not the first, `Timeout` (#600 part 3)
both events of `…06` satisfy the condition: the last, `IOError`, is projected (#600 part 3)
only the first event of `…06` satisfies: `Timeout`, not the last stored `IOError` (#600 part 3)
both links of `…06` satisfy: the last, `child_of`, not the first, `follows_from` (#600 part 3)
an event intrinsic only the first of `…06`'s two events (10 ms) satisfies, not the last (20 ms) (#600 part 3)
a duration threshold read in seconds: the first bucket (3 s) passes, the second (1 s) fails; left in nanoseconds nothing passes (#600 part 1b-1)
the comparison before the ranking: ranked first, the second bucket's top (`edge`, 0.25) fails and leaves nothing (#600 part 1b-1)
a dense zero that fails the comparison is not ranked: the first bucket answers `checkout`, not a zero series (#600 part 1b-1)
a `by()` key held as a string, as a boolean, and by most spans not at all: three series, the last labelled `nil` (#600 part 1b-1)
a value aggregation over one span, `…09` in the second bucket: one sample and none at the first label, where a dense series would carry 0 (#600 part 1b-1)
an attribute target, unscaled: `…01`'s 1500 alone in the first bucket, `…02`'s 900 in the second; spans without `bytes` are not counted (#600 part 1b-1)
a `span:childCount` target: each bucket sums its spans' direct children, a leaf counting 0 (#600 part 1b-1)
an intrinsic `by()` key, labelled `name` (#600 part 1b-1)
two levels: the second bucket's p0.5 is the 5th of 9 durations, p0.9 the 9th; its exemplar (3 s) sits on p0.9, the first bucket's single span ties and sits on p0.5 (#600 part 1b-1)
more exemplar candidates than the budget: three kept by an even stride in bucket order, then series order (#600 part 1b-2)
the same stride over a comparison's candidates, keys in order, baseline before selection (#600 part 1b-2)
a filter that names an event field: still no event or link key (C9; #600 part 1b-2)
an ungrouped rate no span matches: one series of zeros on both routes (#600 part 1b-2)
an aggregation no span matches: no series on either route (#600 part 1b-2)
the threshold on the instant route: the window's longest span (3 s) passes 2 s, and fails it left in nanoseconds (#600 part 1b-2)
arrays projected: two strings, empty, one string, two integers; a mixed array projects nothing
arrays as `by()` keys
presence: every array but the mixed one
arrays are not counted in `compare()`
an array `by()` key on the metrics routes: each array its own `nil` series, the mixed one with the spans that lack the key
a mixed array on a well-known key: one `nil` series with the spans that lack the key
an integer against an array: any element (#493)
`!=` against an array: any number element differing; a span lacking the key never (#493)
an ordered comparison against an array: any element, which the first element alone would not answer (#493)
a double against an array of doubles (#493)
an ordered string comparison against an array (#493)
a regex against an array: string elements only (#493)
`!~` against an array: any string element not matching (#493)
a boolean against an array (#493)
an event attribute holding an array (#493)
a link attribute holding an array (#493)
a resource attribute holding an array (#493)
an unscoped key reaching a resource array (#493)
a key holding a scalar and arrays in one part, as a `by()` key (#493)
the same key and an event key holding a scalar and an array, projected (#493)
an aggregate over the same key: arrays skipped (#493)
array membership on the metrics routes (#493)
string membership in an array: the stored array is projected, not the literal (#493)
`!=` is any string differing: `["x","y"]` and `["z"]` match; an empty array, an integer array, the mixed array and a span lacking the key do not (#493)
a `status` or `kind` keyword against an attribute matches no span (#493)
